title: Correcting Systematic and State-Dependent Errors in the NOAA FV3-GFS Using Neural Networks
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
parameterization_target: analysis increments / systematic model error tendencies for temperature, specific humidity, and horizontal winds
code_availability: The source code for the FV3-GFS model can be found at https://github.com/ufs-community/ufs-weather-model. The data assimilation and replay workflows are available at https://github.com/jswhit/da_scripts and https://github.com/jswhit/replay_scripts. The data reduction and training scripts are available at https://github.com/NOAA-PSL/model_error_correction.
testbed_rationale: While the training and workflow scripts are open on GitHub, the multi-terabyte replay output dataset itself is not hosted in a permanent public data repository or downloadable cloud archive.
pain_points: Language/framework interface barrier: interfacing Fortran FV3-GFS with Python ML required stop-and-restart execution with intermediate files every 6 hours, creating an operational bottleneck.
Low signal-to-noise ratio in training data: analysis increments conflate systematic model error with observational network heterogeneity, measurement noise, and initial condition errors.
Resolution transferability: 2D CNN kernels trained on T21 could not be directly executed on C192, necessitating spectral truncation and zero-padding upscaling pipelines.

Generalization breakdown for specific variables: u-wind showed skill offline but degraded online forecast performance in upper atmospheric levels, indicating state-dependent increments contained confounding non-model-error information.
extraction_notes: Robert Pincus was supported via NSF STC Learning the Earth with Artificial Intelligence and Physics (LEAP), NSF Award 2019625. Online coupling was achieved at 6-hour discrete intervals via intermediate forecast files.
